problem: Improve a small classifier on sklearn.load_digits (1797 handwritten8x8 digit images) under label-preserving corruptions: additive pixel noise and random pixel dropout. Use fixed stratified train/validation/test split, fit preprocessing on train only, reserve test for final evaluation, and compare a standardized RBF-SVM plus ordinary corruption augmentation. Optimize mean accuracy across clean and fixed corruption severities under 5 CPU minutes on an Apple Silicon laptop, no pretrained models or external data. Propose a distinct implementable intervention and ablation; do not merely list known techniques or claim external novelty.

proposal.title: Gaussian Pre-Smoothing for Corruption-Robust RBF-SVM on 8×8 Digits
proposal.intervention: Apply a fixed 2D Gaussian blur (σ tuned on validation from {0.0, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1.0}) to every 8×8 image before StandardScaler and RBF-SVM. The blur is fit-free and applied identically at train, validation, and test time. Augmentation with corrupted copies is added during training only.
proposal.mechanism: Additive pixel noise and dropout inject high-spatial-frequency variance that inflates RBF kernel distances unpredictably. Gaussian smoothing low-pass filters each image, attenuating pixel-scale perturbations while retaining 2–4 pixel stroke structure that carries digit identity at this resolution. After smoothing, StandardScaler normalizes residual variance so gamma='scale' operates on a stable feature distribution. The result is that corrupted and clean versions of the same digit map to closer points in feature space, reducing intra-class kernel distance variance without discarding discriminative structure.
proposal.assumptions: Corruptions are predominantly high-spatial-frequency relative to digit strokes. At 8×8 resolution, digit strokes span roughly 2–4 pixels, so σ≤0.8 attenuates noise without merging strokes. If dominant corruptions were low-frequency (global brightness shift) or σ exceeded ~1.0, clean accuracy would degrade as strokes merge, invalidating the mechanism.
proposal.baseline: StandardScaler plus RBF-SVM (C=10, gamma='scale') with corruption augmentation during training and no pre-smoothing (σ=0). This is the direct comparison: same pipeline, same augmentation, only smoothing absent.
proposal.metric: Mean classification accuracy averaged across six conditions evaluated on the held-out validation set during tuning, then once on the test set: clean data, noise_std=0.3, noise_std=0.6, dropout_p=0.1, dropout_p=0.3, and combined noise_std=0.3 plus dropout_p=0.2. Single final test evaluation after σ is selected.
proposal.falsification: If σ=0 matches or exceeds all σ>0 on the six-condition validation average, the high-frequency noise mechanism is falsified and smoothing provides no causal benefit. Additionally, if clean-only accuracy at optimal σ drops more than two percentage points below σ=0, over-smoothing has destroyed discriminative structure, also falsifying the claim of a beneficial operating range.
proposal.implementation: Load digits, create stratified 60/20/20 train/val/test split with fixed random state. For each σ in {0.0, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1.0}: reshape each train image to 8×8, apply gaussian_filter, ravel; fit StandardScaler on smoothed train features; augment train set with corrupted copies (noise and dropout); fit SVC(kernel='rbf', C=10, gamma='scale'); evaluate six-condition mean accuracy on smoothed validation set. Select σ maximizing validation mean. Refit on train plus validation with chosen σ, evaluate once on test. Total runtime under two minutes on Apple Silicon.
